[简体中文](README.md) | **English**

> Open-source tools for live captions, interpreting, AI meeting notes, dictation and transcribing recordings. Each entry shows the systems it supports, whether it runs fully local, whether it needs your own API key and whether it is Chinese-friendly. Stars refresh weekly.

Online classes, meetings, foreign-language streams and writing all depend on turning speech into text. Open-source speech-to-text tools have moved fast in the past few months: some add live bilingual captions to anything that's playing, some write meeting notes without putting a bot in the call, some let you hold a key and speak instead of typing, and many run entirely on your own computer so recordings never leave it.

This list sorts these tools by task and shows, for each one, the systems it supports, whether it runs fully local, whether it needs your own API key and whether it is Chinese-friendly.

69 projects · data refreshed 2026-11-16

<a id="rules"></a>
## Good to know

> [!IMPORTANT]
> - **Local or cloud.** Tools marked 🔒 can run entirely on your device, so recordings are not uploaded. Tools marked 🔑 need your own API key, send audio or text to the provider you choose, and may cost money.
> - **Ask before you record.** Many countries and regions require consent from everyone being recorded, and companies and schools may have their own rules. Tell people before you record and transcribe a meeting or class.
> - **Hardware.** Local models can be heavy on memory and GPU. Some Mac apps only run locally on Apple Silicon (MacParakeet, for example; Cicada is fully on-device only there, and newer Buzz releases dropped Intel Macs); Meetily's Windows installer needs an AVX2 CPU; without a dedicated GPU, try the CPU-only hayamimi or a smaller model.
> - **Chinese.** Start with tools marked 🀄; many use Alibaba's FunASR, SenseVoice or Qwen3-ASR models. The Tingo author notes FunASR handles Chinese punctuation, numbers and names better than general English-first models.

This list does not include "stealth" interview or exam cheating assistants, or tools pitched at secret recording or invading privacy.

**Legend**: 🔒 Runs fully local (audio stays on your device) · 🔑 Needs your own API key · 🀄 Chinese-friendly (Chinese UI or docs, or built for Chinese use) · 🆕 Created in the last 60 days · 💤 No update for over a year · 📦 Archived

> [!NOTE]
> Labels and supported systems come from each project's README and are only shown when the README says so; a missing label doesn't mean no. Listed means the README was checked, not that recognition quality was tested.

## Live captions and interpreting

Listen to whatever your computer or phone is playing and add live captions or translations to lectures, meetings, streams and foreign videos, with no bot joining the call.

- **[LiveCaptions-Translator](https://github.com/SakiRinn/LiveCaptions-Translator)** · ★ 4.1k<br>Windows Live Captions plus a translation API: accurate, lightweight system captions with LLM translation, no Copilot+ PC required.<br><sub>Windows · updated 2026-08 · Apache-2.0</sub><br><sub>💡 Requires Windows 11</sub>
- **[cicada](https://github.com/wquguru/cicada)** · ★ 2.3k · 🀄 🆕<br>Cicada: live bilingual captions, interpreting and structured notes for any meeting or stream, from Tencent Meeting and Feishu to Zoom and YouTube; hold a key and the other side hears your words translated.<br><sub>macOS / Windows / Linux / Android · updated 2026-11 · Apache-2.0</sub><br><sub>💡 Fully on-device on Apple Silicon Macs; see the README for other platforms</sub>
- **[LiveCaptions](https://github.com/abb128/LiveCaptions)** · ★ 1.8k · 🔒 💤<br>Live captions for the Linux desktop from desktop or mic audio, which is never sent anywhere.<br><sub>Linux · updated 2025-02 · GPL-3.0</sub><br><sub>💡 English only for now</sub>
- **[LiveTranslate](https://github.com/TheDeathDragon/LiveTranslate)** · ★ 914 · 🔑<br>Real-time audio translation for Windows: captures system audio and the mic, recognizes speech locally and translates through an LLM API in a transparent overlay.<br><sub>Windows · updated 2026-08 · MIT</sub>
- **[Mimi](https://github.com/yuxino/Mimi)** · ★ 888 · 🔑<br>Adds live translated captions to whatever video, stream or class is playing; it can listen to a single app and export captions as notes, and saves nothing by default.<br><sub>macOS / Windows / Linux / Android · updated 2026-11 · MIT</sub><br><sub>💡 Apple Silicon Macs on macOS 26+ can use on-device Apple speech; otherwise you need your own provider key</sub>
- **[auto-caption](https://github.com/HiMeditator/auto-caption)** · ★ 610 · 🔒 🀄<br>A cross-platform live caption overlay that runs local models such as Vosk and SenseVoice, with optional translation through Ollama or online APIs.<br><sub>Windows / macOS / Linux · updated 2026-10 · MIT</sub>
- **[v2s](https://github.com/franklioxygen/v2s)** · ★ 513 · 🔒<br>A macOS menu-bar bilingual caption bar that can capture a single app, using Apple's on-device speech and translation, with summaries.<br><sub>macOS · updated 2026-10</sub>
- **[hayamimi](https://github.com/oboroge0/hayamimi)** · ★ 464 · 🔒<br>Multilingual real-time transcription on CPU only: live subtitles, a browser dashboard, speaker labels and translation, with no GPU or cloud API.<br><sub>updated 2026-09</sub>
- **[AudioScript](https://github.com/niyongsheng/AudioScript)** · ★ 376 · 🔒 🀄 🆕<br>AudioScript turns system audio from podcasts, videos and meetings into floating bilingual captions, with recognition and translation done on your machine.<br><sub>macOS / Windows / Linux · updated 2026-11 · MIT</sub>
- **[simul-subtitle](https://github.com/KorenKrita/simul-subtitle)** · ★ 119 · 🔑 🆕<br>Floating live-interpreting captions for Japanese and English videos and streams over any player; recognition runs offline on the device and translation uses your own LLM key.<br><sub>Android / macOS / Windows · updated 2026-10 · MIT</sub>

<a id="faq"></a>
## FAQ

**Which one is most accurate?**
It depends on the language, accent and recording quality, and this list has not run a common benchmark. For Chinese, start with FunASR or SenseVoice-based tools; for English, tools built on Whisper and Parakeet are the most common.

**Can it hear the other people on Zoom or Teams?**
Most live caption and meeting-note tools record the computer's system audio, so they hear everyone without adding a bot to the call; the Cicada, Yogurt and Tingo READMEs all say so. Phones generally don't allow recording other apps' call audio, and Cicada suggests using speaker mode with its face-to-face mode.

**Does it cost anything?**
Everything here is open source and free to run locally; cloud APIs are billed by the provider. VoiceInk's official builds are paid, but you can build it from source.

**How often are stars updated?**
Every Monday GitHub Actions refreshes the stars and re-sorts the list, and links are checked weekly.

<a id="finder"></a>
## Let your AI agent pick

This list is also a skill. Install the [`skills/transcription-finder`](skills/transcription-finder) folder in your AI agent (or run `npx skills add DU8866-nice/awesome-ai-transcription`) and ask:

> I'm on a Windows laptop and want free live English captions for my online lectures. Which tool should I use?

It picks two or three entries for your system, task, budget and privacy needs, explains why, and reminds you to get consent before recording.
